headline: Meta Discovers AI Efficiency: Fire 10% of Staff
subheadline: Nothing says 'we have a plan' like trimming the payroll to justify yesterday's board presentation.
source_headline: Meta to lay off 8,000 as part of AI efficiency push
body_html:
Meta announced Thursday it will eliminate approximately 8,000 employees—roughly 10% of its workforce—in what the company describes as an "AI efficiency push." Translation: the AI spending bender that was supposed to generate returns has instead pressured margins enough that shareholder reassurance now requires bodies on the chopping block. Funny how efficiency means "fewer people doing the same AI work we said we needed all these people to do."

The timing is exquisite. Meta spent years expanding headcount to build its metaverse vision, AI infrastructure, and various moonshots that promised to reshape civilization. Now those same ambitious narratives require the inverse narrative: we were bloated. The company that convinced investors it needed massive AI expenditures is now asking those same investors to trust that 8,000 fewer employees won't materially impact the AI roadmap that justified the spending in the first place. Margin protection disguised as strategic vision.

The company's language is chef's kiss corporate euphemism. "Efficiency push" means we hired too many people relative to our ability to monetize their output. "Reassure investors" means our stock needs a bump and we're willing to borrow from next quarter's earnings to buy this one. The cuts "underscore how soaring AI costs are pressuring even the biggest tech companies"—which is to say, the emperor's new clothes are very expensive and someone finally noticed.

Meta proved one thing conclusively: you can burn capital at any scale and call it a strategy, right up until the moment you can't. Then it's called restructuring.
glossary_definition: A corporate downsizing dressed up as technological optimization, deployed when investor confidence requires the appearance of prudent cost management.
